evidence.title: Application activity increases do not themselves measure useful output
evidence.observation: Source-reported finding: In telemetry from eleven companies, Yu and colleagues estimate that frequent Copilot users increased productivity-application actions by 21.2% and communication actions by 7.1%. The measured units are application actions. Observation period and measurement context: January–September 2024; ten weeks before and twenty after enablement.
evidence.evidence_standing: Source-reported bounded account; study or measurement; not independently reproduced
evidence.glossary_fit: Unmatched: relevant work-allocation evidence retained without forcing a glossary term

source_locations.SRC-124: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.15550v1 — methods, results, figures and limitations

evidence.limitations: Activity is not output quality, time saved or productivity itself. Adoption selection remains. Reduced email activity may remove redundancy or reduce information exchange; these interpretations are not resolved by action counts.
evidence.open_questions: Transfer to other populations, tasks and operating environments remains unestablished. Missing measurement details are not inferred.
evidence.support_assessment: Commons interpretation: A relevant work-allocation measurement retained without a forced glossary connection.
